:::{#thm-first-order-condition}
#### First-order necessary condition

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$.
If $\vx^*$ is a [local minimizer](algebra.qmd#def-local-minimizer) of $f$
and the gradient of $f$ exists at $\vx^*$,
then $\vx^*$ is a stationary point of $f$ (@def-stationary-point).

:::

::: proof

Take $\tolin > 0$ as in the definition of a local minimizer.
Let $i \in \cb{1, \ldots, p}$,
let $\vecf{e}_i$ be the vector with $1$ in entry $i$ and $0$ elsewhere,
and let $g_i(t) \eqdef f(\vx^* + t\,\vecf{e}_i)$ for $t \in \reals$.
For $\abs{t} < \tolin$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\norm{(\vx^* + t\,\vecf{e}_i) - \vx^*} &= \abs{t}\,\norm{\vecf{e}_i} \\
&= \abs{t} \\
&< \tolin,
\end{aligned}
$$

so

$$
\begin{aligned}
g_i(0) &= f(\vx^*) \\
&\le f(\vx^* + t\,\vecf{e}_i) \\
&= g_i(t):
\end{aligned}
$$

$0$ is a local minimizer of $g_i$.
Moving $\vx$ from $\vx^*$ along $\vecf{e}_i$ changes only $x_i$,
so $g_i'(0)$ is the partial derivative $\deriv{x_i} f(\vx^*)$,
which exists because the gradient does.
By @thm-fermat,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{x_i} f(\vx^*) &= g_i'(0) \\
&= 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $g_i'(0) = 0$ holds for every $i$, so every entry of the [gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative) at $\vx^*$ is $0$.

:::
